data.long_meaning: Ramavatar translates to 'Rama's Protector' in Sanskrit and Hindi. 'Rama' refers to the popular Hindu deity, Lord Rama, who embodies the ideals of righteousness, duty, and love. 'Vatar' means protector or guardian. This name is often given to a boy as a symbol of strength, courage, and divine protection. The name Ramavatar carries the meaning “God's Name, Rama's Protector” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ramavatar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's name, rama's protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ramavatar was a title conferred upon Ramachandra, a renowned king of the Solar Dynasty in Hindu mythology. He is most famously known as Lord Rama, the hero of the Indian epic Ramayana.

Ramavatar II was a Rajput king of the Chauhan dynasty in the 12th century AD, who ruled over the regions of Gujarat and Malwa in present-day India. He is known for his military prowess and is said to have expanded his kingdom significantly during his reign.
